get.description: What the web app needs to know before it can sign in: is a sign-in needed, and does this device still have to be set up.

put.description: Change the device password (the current one is needed when there is one). The caller stays signed in.

schema.description: The current password (when there is one) and the new one.
schema.title: PasswordBody

post.description: Claim a new device: the setup code (from its log or its panel) and the password to choose. Starts a session.

schema.description: The setup code (from the log or the panel) and the password to choose.
schema.title: SetupBody

post.description:
The storage as one encrypted file (`{ "passphrase": ..., "confirm": ... }`, the passphrase of this backup: at least 12 characters, typed twice). Answers the file itself (`application/octet-stream`).
Not a point-in-time snapshot: each file is whole, and they are read while the device runs.

schema.description: The passphrase of this backup, typed twice.
schema.title: BackupBody

post.description: Google's second step: `value` is the address the browser was sent to.
Microsoft's waiting step: `{ done: false, poll }` until the sign-in is finished.
Start signing in the account named `key` (as saved). Always 200: `{ session, message, link?, code?, input?, poll? }` or `{ done, ok: false, message }`.
Ask Comic Vine with the key typed (or the saved one, when the field shows the mask): `{ ok, message }`, always 200, in our words. Never kept. (`/test` is the series' Test.)

get.description: The Gemini image models the saved key may use.
The qualities a Google image part offers: each asks for an image size (a model that does not take it uses the nearest one below).
The Gemini text models the saved key may use, for the Google Text part.
The models the saved key may use: each image model with the ratios and sizes it takes (Google's discovery document), and the text models.

post.description: Ask Google with the key typed (or the saved one, when the field shows the mask): `{ ok, message }`, always 200, in our words. Never kept.

get.description: The image models the saved key may use and the OpenAI Image part can drive (no retired DALL·E).
Every quality an image model takes; a model asked for one it does not take uses the nearest one below it.
The text models the saved key may use, for the OpenAI Text part.
The models the saved key may use: each image model with what it takes (qualities, sizes), and the text models.

post.description: Ask OpenAI with the key typed (or the saved one, when the field shows the mask): `{ ok, message }`, always 200, in our words. Never kept.
Ask OpenWeatherMap with the key typed (or the saved one, when the field shows the mask): `{ ok, message }`. Never kept.
Ask Thunderforest with the key typed (or the saved one, when the field shows the mask): `{ ok, message }`. Never kept.

get.description: What the panel shows now: the last `shown` event, or null before anything was drawn.

post.description:
Show a picture over everything for `minutes`: the request's body is the picture itself (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WEBP, at most 10 MB), `title` and `minutes` are in the address
(`curl -X POST --data-binary @door.jpg -H "Content-Type: image/jpeg" "http://pi/api/display/image?minutes=2"`). It is shown whole, on a blurred margin of its own colors.

get.description: A shown image by its digest, as PNG. The digest only selects among the images kept; it is never a path, and an unknown one is a 404.

post.description: Show `text` (with an optional `title`) over everything for `minutes`. The answer has the `id` that takes it down again (`DELETE /api/display/message/{id}`) and `startsInSeconds`, the least it waits.

delete.description: Take a pushed message or picture down, whether it is showing or still waiting its turn. 404 when there is none (it was never made, or it is over).

get.description: The display devices that are installed (`python/displays`): what the display type's `schema` field chooses among, each with the settings of its own.

schema.title: Response List Locales Api Lookups Locale Get

get.description:
The providers of a capability (#513) that are enabled, for the device's choice of one (`weatherProvider`): a capability of our own list, else a 404.
One that is not set up says so in its name (choosing it is harmless: the device then takes one that is), and `ready` says it for a script.

schema.title: Response List Providers Api Lookups Providers  Capability  Get
Response List Timezones Api Lookups Timezone Get

post.description:
Open a backup (`{ "archive": <base64>, "passphrase": ..., "apply": false|true }`). Without `apply` it only says what would change, by name (the summary the person confirms); with it the files
are written. Every document is checked by the rules of the route that would have saved it; with any problem nothing is written. The device password is never touched (a backup does not hold it), and
nothing is deleted: a file in the storage that the backup does not have stays.

schema.description: The backup file (base64), its passphrase, and whether to write it (without, only what would change).
schema.title: RestoreBody

get.description:
The timer task triggers for each of `days` days, starting on the day of `start` (today by default).
Disabled items are not rendered (the timer layer does not run them); items whose trigger is malformed are skipped and listed in `invalid`.

parameters.description: The first day: YYYY-MM-DD (that calendar day), or a time with an offset or Z (its day in the system time zone). A time without an offset is a 422.
parameters.name: start

schema.description: The first day: YYYY-MM-DD (that calendar day), or a time with an offset or Z (its day in the system time zone). A time without an offset is a 422.
schema.title: Start

post.description:
Present the API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or the device password as `{ "password": "..." }`. When it is right, the server
starts a session and sets the session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, so scripts cannot read it and other sites cannot send it).

schema.description: The device password; the API token is a Bearer header instead, with no body.
schema.title: SignInBody

get.description:
The factory values of a device-wide document, from the copy shipped in the NVE (not the stored schema's, and not the stored document): what a "restore the
default" button puts back in the form (the user saves it, or not). Only values, never the stored document's `_id` or `_rev`.
Whether the display and the two layers came up: `{ ok, components: { name: { state: ok|failed|starting, message } } }`. Our words only.

Numbers and our own words only: no host name, address, user or path. `pi` is present only on a Raspberry Pi. A reading the machine cannot give is left out.
The storage's folders are walked on every call (a few dozen small files); the page asks every ten seconds while it is open.

post.description: A rough position from the device's public IP address, for the Location field's button: `{ ok, message, latitude?, longitude? }`. Nothing is saved; always 200, in our words.

get.description: The kept events newer than `since`, oldest first (a first paint, a script, or catching up).

post.description:
The roles of the palette for these theme settings (what the form holds, saved or not): `[{ name, color }]`, name as the CSS class, color as `hsl()`.
Values that are not valid read as the factory defaults, as they do on the device.

get.description: Whether playback is stopped, for the play/stop button.

post.description:
Forward a command: `play` (resume where it stopped), `stop`, or `next` (the next track; a stopped layer plays from there).
It is accepted, not done: the layer does it on its own thread, and its telemetry says what happened.
